title: Mehmed II Makes the Anti-Union Monk Gennadios Patriarch
dek: On 6 January 1454 the sultan who took Constantinople installs its leading foe of union with Rome as patriarch. Later sultans repeat the investiture for the patriarchs after him.
body: The sultan handed the new patriarch his staff himself. Later accounts called it the birth of a millet system; historians doubt one existed in 1454.

panels.label: Gennadios Said
panels.text: Gennadios told the people of Constantinople that by forsaking their faith and trusting the Italians instead of God, they would lose their city.

panels.label: Bessarion Said
panels.text: Bessarion said he urged union with Rome because he found no error in Latin doctrine, and would have suffered the worst before counseling it out of fear for the body.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Each side said it defended the true faith; at stake was who would protect and govern the Orthodox once Byzantium fell, a patriarch under the sultan or a Church joined to Rome.
